result.title: 3 OpenClaw Setup That Will 10x Your Output
result.description:
Three OpenClaw setups that will change how much you can get done, and I'll drop the exact prompts so you can set these up yourself.

Quick reminder before anything, only do this if you understand how permissions and security work. OpenClaw is powerful, and you want to know what you're handing it access to. 

First — Custom Mission Control. This is your home base. Instead of OpenClaw being a general-purpose agent, you set it up with a specific mission - your goals, your priorities, your workflows, your preferences. Think of it like onboarding a new team member, except you write the onboarding doc yourself. The more specific you are about how you work and what matters, the more useful every single interaction becomes. This one setup changes everything downstream.

Second — Discord Setup. You connect OpenClaw to your Discord, and it becomes an active participant in your server, monitoring channels, flagging things that need your attention, and executing tasks based on what's happening in real time. If your team lives in Discord, this turns OpenClaw from a tool you go to into something that's already in the room with you.

Third — Multi-Agent Framework. Instead of one agent doing everything, you set up multiple specialized agents that each handle a specific type of task - one for research, one for file management, one for communications and they work in parallel. The output you can get from a well-structured multi-agent setup is genuinely hard to believe until you see it running.

All three of these prompts are linked in the video description, grab them and try it yourself.

Which setup are you starting with? Drop it in the comments 👇

result.title: 3 Claude Cowork Features That Will Change How You Use It
result.description:
If you've been using Claude Cowork, these are the three features that will completely change how you use it:

First - Skills. This is the one that makes Cowork feel like it was built specifically for you. Skills are essentially custom commands you can trigger to get Claude to do very specific things the way you want them done. Once you set these up they become muscle memory. You stop typing long prompts and start just telling it what you need in one word.

Second - Connectors. You can connect it to the tools you're already using - Gmail, Google Drive, Slack, Notion, Google Calendar, and Claude can actually read and work across all of them at the same time. So when you ask it to prep you for a meeting, it's not just working with what you tell it in the chat. It's pulling from your actual emails, your actual calendar, your actual documents. The context it has access to completely changes the quality of what it can do for you.

Third - Scheduled Tasks. You can tell Cowork to do something at a specific time - run a daily digest every morning, pull a report every Friday, follow up on something next week. You set it once, and it runs without you having to think about it again. This is the closest thing to having an assistant that works while you sleep.

The combination of all three is what makes Cowork feel different from just chatting with AI. It's less of a tool you use and more of a system that works around you.

Which one are you trying first? Drop it in the comments 👇

result.title: Stop Watching AI Slop Build These Projects Instead
result.description:
If your feed looks anything like mine right now, it is full of AI content. And a lot of it is the same thing recycled over and over with a new thumbnail.
So here's what I'd actually build instead of watching another top 10 AI tools video:

Build a personal finance tracker that reads your actual statements and automatically categorizes your spending. You'll use it every month.
Build an email agent that triages your inbox and drafts responses for the ones that follow a pattern. You'll feel the time savings immediately.
Build a research tool that takes a topic, pulls sources, and gives you a summary you can actually trust. Every time you need to learn something new, it's already there.

The difference between people who are getting better at AI and people who just know a lot about AI is the building. That's it. That's the whole gap.

Pick one. Start today.

result.title: Canceling Subscriptions, Building Local AI Agents
result.description:
I've been on a cancellation spree lately.

There are tools I was paying for monthly that I realized I could just build myself, better, more specific to what I actually need, and free to run after the initial build.

The one that started it was accounting software. I was paying for something that handled maybe 80% of what I needed, and the other 20% was always a workaround. So I built my own using open-source AI, hosted locally.
And then I started looking at everything else the same way. What am I paying for that's only 80% of what I need? What's too specific for any company to build for me?

The answer was more things than I expected.

Local agents are more accessible than people think right now. You don't need a huge technical background to get started. And the privacy angle alone, keeping your data on your own machine, is worth it for certain workflows.
What's a subscription you have that you've thought about replacing? Drop it in the comments 👇
